title: Cut over to records-only attribution at C0 and stop trailers
summary: Job 7 part 1 of the records-history plan: pick C0 as main's tip, run the importer and write the legacy-exempt record to athena/records, make `athena check --attribution` use the legacy rule up to C0 and records only after, and stop writing Athena trailers on new landings. Audience: the maintainer and the verifier, who judge by `athena check --attribution` on main and by a new landing's message. The reader moves of §13 (the second half of job 7) are not part of this part.

defaults_applied.how: cargo test and clippy criteria cover the legacy/records split and the no-trailer landing.
Behavior criteria run `athena check --attribution` and a landing.
Criteria check verdicts and message contents, not that wiring exists.
The decisions entry gives C0 and the reasoning for an outside reader.
No secrets or personal data in the records or the decision entry.
The import count is measured by the importer's self-check.
Readers' move is deferred so the change stays one cutover.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Job 6 (3d947a7) is already on main, so C0 is main's tip when the run starts. Its full sha is recorded in docs/decisions.md.
The importer and the legacy_exempt_change writer already exist from jobs 2 and 5; this job calls them and wires `check_attribution_with_legacy` into `athena check --attribution`.
Trailer-writing sites are in athena-core (run.rs, steward.rs, proposals.rs, work_decisions.rs). Trailer readers for pre-cutover history stay.
Moving the readers of §13 to a worktree of athena/records is a later part and is out of scope. records/ stays on main and [history] exempt stays in athena.toml until job 8.
ci.yml makes the attribution check required (and the pr-head job) per §10 item 7. Governance files such as athena.toml are not changed.
Pushing athena/records is an operational step. The code and tests must make the import and the cutover repeatable, and the run does them once.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`: both pass. Tests show a commit at or before C0 judged by the legacy rule, with the seven named commits handled as §4 says, and a commit after C0 judged by records only.
Run `athena check --attribution` on main after the cutover: it passes. The verifier may run it with `cargo run -- check --attribution`.
A test (or `cargo run`) that creates a landing in a scratch repository produces a commit message with no `Athena-` trailer lines, and the landing is still attributed by its records.

The athena/records branch holds the import commit, with every file of records/ at C0 and import-manifest.json. The self-check passed (path count and SHA-256 equal to C0), and the output or decision entry reports the measured file count.
legacy-exempt.json on athena/records holds the six athena.toml entries plus 02837e0, each with the reason from the athena.toml comments.
docs/decisions.md has an entry recording C0's full sha, the import commit, the legacy-exempt record, the switch of the required check, and the end of trailers. It cites D111 and design §4 and §10.
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` makes the attribution check a blocking job after the cutover. The pr-head job becomes required if §10 job 4 says so.
Pre-cutover trailer readers (the status and auditor greps) still work on old commits, and no trailer-free landing is misread as unattributed.

out_of_scope: Moving the readers of §13 (Records::load, RecordSet::load, read_records) to a worktree of athena/records
Removing records/ from main or emptying [history] exempt in athena.toml (job 8)
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or other governance files
departures: The job touches several crates plus CI and an operational import/push, so cost and time are above the reference. Verification is harder because the verifier cannot write or push.
